newsitem.title: USA: 3Com falls on earnings shortfall forecast.
newsitem.headline: 3Com falls on earnings shortfall forecast.

text.p: 3Com Corp shares fell more than 20 percent Monday after the networking equipment maker said earnings for its fiscal third quarter would fall short of Wall Street estimates.
Analysts said 3Com, the second-largest U.S. networking vendor, could face even more quarters of weak results because of rising competition from Intel Corp.
In late-morning trading, 3Com shares were off 10-5/8 to 40-1/8 on Nasdaq trading volume of 14.7 million shares, making it the most active stock in U.S. markets.
3Com said it expected revenue for the third quarter, ending February 28, of $770-$810 million, and per-share earnings of $0.45-$0.50.
According to First Call, the consensus Wall Street forecast is $0.60 a share.
Three weeks ago, 3Com executives told analysts that revenue was unexpectedly weak in December but picked up in January. The news sparked a three-week decline in the stock.

Last week Intel sharply cut prices of its fast ethernet cards, the components that connect personal computers to networks. That forced 3Com to announce today that it too would cut prices of its ethernet products, where it gets about 43 percent of its revenue.
"3Com is the industry leader" in ethernet cards, said Peter Lieu, analyst at brokerage Adams, Harkness & Hill. "They could have said we are not going to do anything, but they responded."
3Com is also losing ground on more expensive networking products, such as switches, to its biggest rival Cisco Systems Inc, analysts said.

3Com's earnings forecast raised concern about the entire networking industry, whose revenues have been growing about 35 percent annually. 3Com's woes are a sign that the industry's revenue growth is finally slowing, analysts said.
Shares of Cisco also fell, down 4-3/4 to 58-3/8. Ascend Communications Inc, another closely watched networking vendor, fell 5-5/8 to 61-5/8, and Cabletron Systems Inc fell two points to 28-7/8.
